## Overview

This is the release-QC companion to the [SVD/WP compression benchmark](index.qmd): where that
page derives and calibrates the codec, this one validates the actual shipped **v03 Brain-Wide
Map (BWM) release** — 699 recordings, both the default (ε=150, α=28) and aggressive (ε=450,
α=96) compression passes — against the dataset it replaces on S3 (referred to here as **v00**).

Three things are checked:

1. **The survival-floor fix** (`floor_k=64`, see [index.qmd §Adaptive WP threshold
   calibration](index.qmd#adaptive-wp-threshold-calibration)) actually eliminates the
   zero-damage failure mode in the shipped data, with no regressions.
2. **Saturation detection and muting** — an entirely new pipeline stage in v03, absent from
   v00 — is present and correctly labelled across the release.
3. **Release-wide RMSE / CR** fall in the expected range across all 699 recordings, not just
   the 11 benchmark PIDs used to calibrate ε/α.

## Zero-damage fix: v00 vs v03

Before the fix, low-SNR chunks could be over-thresholded at the wavelet-packet stage until
*every* coefficient of the dominant SVD row was discarded, reconstructing to exact zero —
silently destroying real (if weak) LFP. The root cause and fix are detailed in
[index.qmd](index.qmd#adaptive-wp-threshold-calibration); this section confirms it holds at
release scale.

**Method.** A chunk decompresses to exact zero iff every coefficient of `Vh_hat` was
thresholded away, which is visible directly from the stored `vh_indices` dataset length —
no decompression needed. For each of the 699 BWM recordings, in both the live (v00) and new
(v03) archive, the zero-time fraction was computed as `Σ(chunk length where n_kept==0) /
Σ(chunk length)`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

zd_default = pd.read_csv(
    "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-olivier-PycharmProjects-ephys-atlas-packages-lfpack/"
    "5405c415-e8b2-4fa0-9a31-d183550a3e8a/scratchpad/zero_damage_v00_vs_v03.csv"
)
zd_aggressive = pd.read_csv(
    "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-olivier-PycharmProjects-ephys-atlas-packages-lfpack/"
    "5405c415-e8b2-4fa0-9a31-d183550a3e8a/scratchpad/zero_damage_v00_vs_v03_aggressive.csv"
)

def summary_row(df, label):
    return {
        "pass": label,
        "overall zero-time (v00)": f"{df['n_zero_samples_v00'].sum() / df['ns_total_v00'].sum():.2%}",
        "overall zero-time (v03)": f"{df['n_zero_samples_v03'].sum() / df['ns_total_v03'].sum():.2%}",
        "recordings affected (v00)": int((df["zero_fraction_v00"] > 0).sum()),
        "recordings affected (v03)": int((df["zero_fraction_v03"] > 0).sum()),
        "regressions (v03 worse)": int((df["delta"] > 1e-6).sum()),
    }

pd.DataFrame([summary_row(zd_default, "default"), summary_row(zd_aggressive, "aggressive")])
```

Zero-time-fraction dropped to **exactly 0.00%** across all 699 recordings in both passes, with
**zero regressions** — no recording is worse in v03 than in v00. The worst pre-fix offenders
(up to 99.8% zero-time in the default pass, i.e. essentially the entire recording silently
discarded) are now fully recovered:

![Survival-floor fix: the 15 recordings with the highest pre-fix zero-time fraction, before (v00) and after (v03), both compression passes. Every v03 bar is exactly zero.](figures/2026-07-24_bwm_zero_damage_before_after.png){.lightbox}

Two recordings (`4037a618…`, `46630957…`) are **not** part of this fix: both have
`frac_bad = 1.0` (all 384 channels flagged bad by bad-channel detection) and were never
zero-time in *either* version — a distinct, expected failure mode (dead/noisy input, not
over-thresholding) already tracked separately in `qc_fully_bad_recordings.csv`. They are
flagged for exclusion from downstream analysis, not for recompression.

## Saturation detection & muting — new in v03

v00 ships **no saturation information at all** — the `/<recording>/saturation` HDF5 group
doesn't exist anywhere in the live archive. v03 adds a full insertion-level saturation
pipeline: ADC-clipped spans are detected on the raw LFP band (before any filtering, so
pre-processing can't obscure the clipping), recorded as a per-recording interval table, and
**muted** — zeroed with a cosine taper — on the decimated output *after* Cadzow denoising. This
"late" re-mute was chosen over an early, pre-filter mute in a 2026-07-21 A/B comparison:
muting the raw traces before the highpass/CAR/decimate/Cadzow chain did not keep the span
clean — those stages leaked residual energy (and spurious CSD sources/sinks) back into it — so
a single re-mute of the final output is both cleaner and cheaper.

```{python}
#| echo: false
df_pid = pd.read_parquet("/Users/olivier/Documents/datadisk/lfp-processing/lfpack/v03_bwm/lfp_qc_per_pid.pqt")

rows = []
for pass_name in ["default", "aggressive"]:
    d = df_pid[df_pid["pass"] == pass_name]
    rows.append({
        "pass": pass_name,
        "recordings with saturation": f"{(d['saturated_fraction'] > 0).sum()} / {len(d)}",
        "mean saturated fraction": f"{d['saturated_fraction'].mean():.2%}",
        "total saturated time": f"{d['total_saturated_sec'].sum() / 3600:.1f} h",
        "total saturated intervals": int(d["n_saturated_intervals"].sum()),
        "correctly labelled muted=True": f"{(d['muted']).sum()} / {len(d)}",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

![Saturation detection across the 699-recording default pass: per-recording saturated-fraction distribution (left) and the 15 most-affected recordings with total saturated seconds labelled (right).](figures/2026-07-24_bwm_saturation_detection.png){.lightbox}

446/699 recordings (64%) have at least one detected saturated interval, totalling ~9.2 hours
out of ~936 hours in the release (mean fraction 0.98%) — concentrated in a long tail of
heavily-clipped insertions (up to 24% saturated) rather than spread evenly; most affected
recordings lose well under 1% of their time. See the
[saturation QC how-to](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/lfpack/how-to/bwm-dataset.html#saturation-qc)
for how to query this per-recording via `LFPackReader.saturation` / `.saturation_summary` /
`.saturation_mask`.

**Labelling fix.** Every recording's saturation table now correctly reports `muted=True`. This
required a fix, not just a rebuild: `compress_bin_to_h5` sets `muted = not
checkpoint_existed` — an honest report of whether *this call* ran the mute step — which
under-reports `False` whenever a build resumes from an already-muted Cadzow checkpoint (the
normal case for this release, since decimation is checkpointed and expensive to redo). The v03
build's own checkpoints were already correctly muted, so the underlying data was never wrong —
but the `muted` label was `False` for all 699 recordings until now. Fixed in two places:
`sdsc-slurms/2026-06-lfpack/compress.py` now forces `muted=True` post-hoc for future reruns
(the checkpoint-reuse guarantee is specific to that driver, so the fix lives there rather than
in `lfpack` itself), and the existing v03 HDF5 attrs + QC parquet were patched in place.

## Release-wide QC (v03, all 699 recordings)

```{python}
#| echo: false
rows = []
for pass_name in ["default", "aggressive"]:
    d = df_pid[df_pid["pass"] == pass_name]
    rows.append({
        "pass": pass_name,
        "median RMSE (µV)": round(d["rmse_mean"].median(), 1),
        "RMSE > 25 µV": f"{(d['rmse_mean'] > 25).sum()} / {len(d)}",
        "median total CR": round(d["cr_total_mean"].median()),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

![Release-wide RMSE and compression-ratio distributions across all 699 BWM recordings, default vs aggressive pass. The dashed line marks the 25 µV design target.](figures/2026-07-24_bwm_release_qc_distributions.png){.lightbox}

The default pass sits at median RMSE ≈15 µV / CR ≈115, consistent with the ε=150/α=28
operating point calibrated on the 11-PID benchmark in [index.qmd](index.qmd); 122/699
recordings (17%) exceed the 25 µV design target in the default pass — expected tail behaviour
on genuinely low-SNR or high-saturation insertions, not a regression (RMSE ≤25 µV was a median
target, not a per-recording guarantee).

**Caveat:** the two fully-bad recordings above report `rmse_mean = 0`, which reads as
suspiciously perfect — it reflects a degenerate all-bad-channel input reconstructing exactly,
not compression quality, and should be excluded before aggregating RMSE across the release.
A further 2 recordings (`30dfb8c6…`, `7441d0df…`) have `frac_bad` between 0.5–0.7 and should be
treated with the same caution.

## Conclusion

The v03 BWM release fixes the zero-damage codec bug across the full dataset with no
regressions, ships a new saturation detection/muting pipeline stage with correctly-labelled
metadata across all 699 recordings, and its release-wide RMSE/CR statistics are consistent
with the benchmark calibration. Both compression passes (`lf_compressed_all_bwm.h5`,
`lf_compressed_aggressive_all_bwm.h5`) were published to
`s3://ibl-brain-wide-map-public/resources/ibl-agent-data/` on 2026-07-24, replacing v00.
